Safari Condo's Largest Camper, the 2027 Alto F2414, It's 24 Feet of Camper and Just Under 3,000 Lbs
20 photos
Photo: Princess Craft RV | YouTube Screenshot
Some travel trailers redefine a class, and today, that’s precisely what we’ll be exploring. It’s the one and only Alto F2414, the largest in Safari Condo’s lineup, a camper from which North Americans can expect a different kind of experience, if they choose to own it.
Most of what the market has to offer looks and feels pretty similar, even across entire classes, so when I explored the F2414 from Safari Condo, a Canadian crew on which we’ve shed light before, I just had to bring it to light.
I mean, it’s not every day that we find a camper that offers 24 feet of space and weighs under 3,000 lbs. dry, 2,944 (1,335 kg) , to be precise, marking as one of the lightest and most spacious out there, space that Safari put to damn good use. Heck, even some SUVs can tow this one.
Photo: Safari Condo Part of how this is made possible has to do with the materials that Safari has chosen to use to built their Alto class. Two sheets of aluminum sandwich with a foam core in the middle make up the shell, and this structure is used from tip to tail on the unit. The roof is not a single piece but still handles a ton of upgrades and features on top since the whole body is supported by an aluminum frame.
While the 2027 F2414 weighs under 3K lbs dry, it does have the ability to handle a total load of 4,500 lbs (2,041 kg), granting us access to a whopping 1,500 lbs of cargo, more than you’ll need out there. But do keep in mind that upgrades and changes you make to your unit will occupy some of this space.
And that’s really where we get to see some Safari Condo magic. One trait of the brand and lineup is that Safari encourages owners to chit-chat with their dealers to select the features they want inside. This holds true for everything from the color of their cushions to the presence of an AC, heater, and even off-grid setup.
Photo: Safari Condo The latter can also be heavily expanded , with the ability to accommodate as much as 520 Ah of lithium power and as much as 530 W of solar on the roof. A 3,000 W inverter is in place as standard.
Then there’s the interior of this bad boy, a space which reminds me of classic or vintage campers in terms of layout, but with a bunch of modern touches. For instance, at each end of the unit lies a lounge, both of which can be converted into bedding spaces, so the choice is yours as to where you sleep and how many folks you bring along.
The largest, however, and the one that Safari designates as the main bedroom is located at the rear and composed of two opposing benches and no table in the middle. A little tabletop can be found right next to the lounge and hiding underneath the end of the kitchen counter.
As for the lounge at the front, while it appears to be as simple as possible, Safari does mention that the table from here can be moved outside and attached to the side of the camper, to be used as an outdoor top which can be used for working, dining, and more, all underneath an awning.
Photo: Safari Condo Each of the lounges inside also include ample storage space underneath the seating, and according to the host of the video below, plumbing and electrical lines can easily be accessed and tended to if needed. These bins can be accessed from the inside and outside.
One little trait about the rear lounge that I want to bring to light is the little mobile pillow that we see. This feature is to be used to help you find comfortable positions on the lounge, but my adult mind can also think of so many more uses for this thing, wink-wink.
The lounges aren’t the only unique space in the F2414 either. Both the kitchen and galley are on a whole new level. Starting with the kitchen, I want to point out the massive countertop that runs from the door of the camper all the way to the bedroom. It’s even bigger than what we find in some motorhomes, and the cabinetry and storage underneath are just as massive.
Photo: Princess Craft RV | YouTube Screenshot The host from Princess Craft might even fit inside one of these drawers if she curled up into a ball. Clearly, they’re not meant for that sort of weight, but you get the idea here. Some are designated as storage for clothing and the like. More storage up above is in place too.
This brings us to the bathroom, a space which is unique in its own right too. Come to find out, this RV is equipped with two separate cubicles. One is for the toilet and vanity, while the second is for the shower. That way, the toilet stays dry at all times but also comes in handy in case one person wants to shower while another go about their morning duties.
Safari Condo also equips this unit with solid heating and hot water, provided by Truma, and coupled with the shell construction, Safari condo mentions that we can tackle weather that falls below zero, as long as we winterize, that is. In all, 26 gallons of freshwater are at our disposal.
Photo: Safari Condo Once we consider features and options like two bike racks, outside shower, anti-sway kits, electric jacks, and countless others, it’s not hard to see that the 2027 Alto F2414 is indeed something else and breaks the mold.
The question is: How much does one of these puppies cost? According to sources, a base model is set to go for CAD70,149, or around $50,100 but dealers rarely sell a basic model, so do expect to drop a bit more. For example, Princess Craft showcases a price tag of as much as $89K. But, that number is crossed out, so we can look forward to paying less than that. Shop around.

This Chinese-Built Explorer Can Handle Up to Eight Months of Self-Sufficient Cruising
45 photos
Photo: Drettmann Yachts
People with a real wanderlust (and deep-enough pockets) have access to some of the most capable and rugged personal explorers ever built – these awesome vessels blur the line between commercial ships and luxury private yachts, and are meant to give their owners a real taste of adventure. One of the finest examples is currently up for grabs, fresh out of a comprehensive refit that has upgraded its looks while keeping the rugged capabilities it was built for.
During the world health pandemic that began in 2020, some ultra-rich yacht owners made waves after enjoying the privilege of sailing off and remaining privately isolated onboard their stunning floating mansions. Beyond the controversy, what stays notable is that certain private yachts, which weren’t even available a few decades ago, have such an impressive autonomy combined with premium comfort that they become off-grid private sanctuaries in their own right.
Avalon is one of the best examples. Launched as part of a transoceanic explorer range, Avalon is both a superb luxury yacht and a rugged vessel built to travel to the most remote places on earth and withstand extensive periods of time on the water with no access to refueling infrastructure and supplies. This is the type of new-generation boat that modern nomads love – it’s like a personal expedition ship with the uncompromising comfort of a luxury yacht.
Originally launched as Mazu (the Chinese deity that patrons over fishermen and sailors), this 2012 explorer was the second hull in the TransOcean explorer range developed by the Shanghai-based Cheoy Lee shipbuilder. The first unit was the 2007 Marco Polo, sporting a striking dark green hull. Mazu was just as striking, with its red hull. Both yachts were designed by the acclaimed Ron Holland, who was commissioned by Roland Sturm.
Photo: Drettmann Yachts Sturm, a German real estate developer, had worked previously with Holland on an Abeking &Rasmussen sailing yacht. When he decided to upgrade to a motor yacht that could explore the world, he commissioned Holland to design it and Cheoy Lee to build it. The family-operated Cheoy Lee was one of the oldest shipyards in China, with a massive experience in commercial ships of various kinds, and that would eventually include luxury yachts as well.
Marco Polo was the first motor yacht designed and built for Roland Sturm, and it quickly became a proven world cruiser, with more than 30,000 nautical miles under its belt just in the first two years. Mazu was intended to be the upgraded version, with more than one meter added to its length, and tankage of more than 65,000 liters. Sturm eventually left the project before it was completed, but Mazu came to life anyway and was quickly sold and renamed Qing.
This 46-meter (150.9 feet) explorer is built for a 6,600-nautical mile range, and it was proven to withstand six to eight months of continuous travel, basically operating as a self-sufficient home away from home. In more than a decade, it has cruised in the Mediterranean, Caribbean, Australia, Alaska, the Atlantic, and many parts of the Pacific, gaining the status of a proven world traveler.
In addition to the rugged build, these capabilities are owed to the unique propulsion system developed by the legendary Ron Holland. The system combines a single Caterpillar 3512B engine with an integrated Schottel drive and separate fuel cells that are housed in a second, dedicated machinery space located forward.
Photo: Drettmann Yachts This second system ensures a unique level of redundancy, meaning that it can produce up to six knots of speed alone, even in the event of a main engine malfunction. Because the retractable Schottel thruster is located separately, it remains safe in the case of any main engine room deficiency, and it’s powerful enough to propel the entire ship back home. Plus, it also improves maneuverability during docking.
The single-engine plus the Schottel drive system was inspired from the world of commercial shipping, where the Cheoy Lee shipyard has used it intensively. Other modifications to improve fuel efficiency were also derived from commercial shipbuilding. Huge storage capacities, as well as a 2.5-ton crane on the foredeck for handling heavy water-toy equipment are also part of Avalon’s mandatory explorer capabilities.
During the original build and testing, it was confirmed that at 12 knots, the explorer burned only 155 liters per hour, which was approximately 35 percent less than a two-engine yacht with a similar displacement volume. In addition to being highly fuel-efficient, the yacht was also equipped with fuel tank capabilities of up to 65,000 liters (17,170 gallons), enough to support its monster range of more than 6,500 nautical miles.
After it changed hands in 2024 and renamed Avalon, the Chinese-built explorer underwent a comprehensive refit that transformed its look. The new owners pumped more than €3 million into the 2025/2026 refit that justifies a current price tag of €16,9 million ($19 million). The most obvious is the hull transformation, which changed from the original red paint to a deep navy blue color with a red boot stripe and white superstructure.
Photo: Drettmann Yachts Some of the biggest upgrades include a rebuilt galley, a rebuilt swim platform, a new awning system, and the overhaul of all three generators. In terms of interior style, the original design was refreshed and modernized with a neutral color palette, but still keeping some of the original Asian-inspired accents.
The original layout was influenced by the technical requirements, which is why is differs from that of a typical motor yacht. The full-beam owner’s suite is located on the aft bridge deck, and the four guest cabins on the lower deck, accommodating up to 11 guests. One of the cabins has a flexible, convertible design that can switch from a gaming room to a nanny cabin. A dedicated cinema and a gym were also added to a multi-functional main salon.
Judging by the elegant color palette and contemporary aesthetic with precious materials such as Macassar ebony veneer and walnut flooring, it would be hard to view this is a rugged world explorer. Still, this is one of the main triumphs of new-generation, purpose-built private explorers: they are every bit as luxurious as conventional pleasure craft, but fully capable of autonomous cruising to remote locations at the same time.
Photo: Drettmann Yachts The nine-month refit, which was the most comprehensive one yet for this 2012 yacht, was finalized this past summer. Avalon emerged from its looking sharp and ready for at least another decade of bold expeditions around the world. The owners who invested heavily in its upgrade are now ready to sell it, asking for $19 million – a hefty sum, but entirely worthy of a self-sufficient home on the water and go-anywhere expedition vessel.

This 4x4 Toyota Hiace Camper Van Gets a Pop-Up Roof and Proves Small Can Still Mean Comfortable
30 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Free Roam Fitouts
I love 4x4 camper van conversions – a good one will offer the freedom of going off the beaten path while still accommodating you in comfort and style. The project I'd like to share with you today does exactly that.
What we have here is a conversion based on a Toyota Hiace. It was designed and built by Free Roam Fitouts, an Australia-based company specializing in van and four wheel drive fit-outs, tailored to the customer's wants and needs. We've covered the company's work here on autoevolution, such as this high-end moto hauler .
You can tell this is a one-of-a-kind Toyota Hiace as soon as you lay eyes on it – it's definitely a head-turner.
Although most of the conversion was done by Free Roam Fitouts, several other Australian companies made important modifications to the van. First off, Bus 4x4 did a 4x4 conversion, transforming an otherwise generic Hiace into an adventure machine. What's more, the van rides on black alloy wheels wrapped in rugged-terrain tires.
Second, The Cruiser Company did all the bar work. At the front, you'll come across a bumper with a massive, aggressive-looking bull bar that comes with a winch. The winch is a super useful addition if you plan to do some more hardcore off-roading by yourself.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Free Roam Fitouts On the opposite end, you'll find a swing-away tire carrier and a swing-away cargo box, both from The Cruiser Company. Underneath, the company installed a utility panel with a power hook-up, an Anderson plug for a solar blanket, a water fill-up point, an ARB air compressor connection, and a trailer plug.
Finally, Headspace Campers added the most significant exterior mod – it replaced the standard roof with a pop-up roof extension. It has zipped windows on the sides and a large solar panel on top. Moreover, gas struts make it easy for you to lift the extension. Other notable upgrades include a Headspace awning and a snorkel.
Slide the entrance open, and an efficiently arranged, welcoming interior will greet you. Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for matte white U-groove walls, green laminated cabinetry, wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring, and some Tasmanian oak elements like the countertops or panels on the bed platform's bottom.
As expected on a van this size, the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, the two areas are separated by part of the kitchen. The builder did leave enough space for you to step over into the cabin.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Free Roam Fitouts The living space is split into three key parts: a kitchen, a seating area, and the sleeping area up top when the roof extension is up.
The kitchen forms an L shape and features a deep stainless steel sink with a cover that matches the countertop, an 85-liter Dometic fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, two drawers, and a Joolca portable toilet with a cover.
On the opposite side, you'll come across a tall cabinet with multiple shelves. On top of it, you get some additional surface area when the roof is raised.
One compartment by the entrance houses an Evakool 50-liter chest-style fridge/freezer on a slide-out. The slide-out also has a pull-out table, perfect to use for cooking. Even better, you can remove the table from its compartment, drop the legs, and use it wherever you want.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Free Roam Fitouts A cabinet underneath the sink houses part of the plumbing system: a Duoetto electric water heater and a water pump. The water you use in the sink drains into a greywater tank mounted underneath the vehicle.
It's truly a game-changer to have the roof raised due to the amount of extra space you have available. Not only will you feel less cramped inside the van, but the most important thing is that you can stand up inside the van.
Setting up the bed is pretty straightforward – you need to use a step to climb up in the tent, drop two panels that are held up by gas struts, and you're good to go.
The seating area takes up the rear part of the interior. It has two benches, one on each side, and a detachable swivel table. Free Roam Fitouts set them at a good height so you can sit on them even when the roof extension isn't up. You'll also notice a Sirocco fan with a light and integrated USB outlets.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Free Roam Fitouts Each bench offers a sizeable drawer for storage that can be opened when the trunk door is up – the drawers can also be accessed from the inside by lifting the hinged tops above them.
The passenger-side bench houses the power system – its highlights are a 400 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W Enerdrive inverter. Three charging sources allow you to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging. Moreover, the other bench integrates an outdoor shower connection.
Integrated into the tall cabinet I mentioned earlier is the "command center" for the rig's utilities. It includes an inverter controller, a battery monitor, a 12V cigarette socket, and a switch panel for the lights, a water pump, and a water heater.
All in all, Free Roam Fitouts turned this into an extremely capable overlanding vehicle, with the help of several other companies. On top of that, you can actually sleep and live comfortably in the van, provided you're fine with the little available space. To be fair, considering how small the interior is, it packs more creature comforts than I expected.

Hyundai Venue and Elantra Recalled for Potentially Loose Lug Nuts
33 photos
Photo: Hyundai
Hyundai Motor America is recalling a bunch of small crossovers and compact sedans in the United States because certain lug nuts may not have been tightened properly. Identified under NHTSA campaign number 26V693, this recall covers the 2026 model year Elantra, Elantra Hybrid, Elantra N, and Venue.
Per the recall documentation, all subject vehicles were produced at the Ulsan complex in South Korea. The largest automobile manufacturing facility in the world employs more than 30,000 workers, produces more than 5,000 vehicles per day, and comprises no fewer than six distinct assembly plants as of 2026.
The lug nuts of these vehicles clamp their wheels to the hubs. If under-torqued, loose nuts can produce abnormal noises and vibration while driving. The worst-case scenario is wheel detachment at high speeds, increasing the risk of a crash. A detached wheel also becomes a rolling hazard for other motorists. The recall population comprises 17 vehicles, beginning with eight units of the Venue.
Produced for model year 2026 between August 11 and August 27, 2026, these crossovers are joined by a single Elantra N , four hybrids, and four gas-only sedans. The Elantra population is listed with assembly dates ranging from August 10 through August 24, 2026. Hyundai's US subsidiary learned about the recall condition back on September 22, 2026.
A temporary manual torquing process at the Ulsan complex is to blame for the improperly fastened lug nuts. After a period of modifications to wheel tightening tooling, the manual tightening process ended on September 16, 2026. Said temporary process was intended to keep vehicle production moving while the tooling change was implemented.
Photo: Hyundai The recall documentation lists part number 52950-14140 for the wheel hub nut assembly, supplied by Samjin Nut of Cheonan. The South Korean automaker says that it's unaware of incidents that may involve the condition stateside. Of course, dealers are to inspect and thoroughly retighten the lug nuts. The repair is free of charge even if the car is no longer covered by the new vehicle limited warranty.
If dealers find something off, the hub bearing assembly will be replaced as well, also at no charge to affected customers. While that may sound excessive, bear in mind that an improperly clamped wheel moves under load. This movement hammers the bearing's precision surfaces, introducing play into the mix. Given the aforementioned, a hub bearing assembly inspection is definitely a must.
Hyundai Motor America intends to notify owners by first-class mail no later than December 19, 2026. Vehicle identification numbers became searchable on the NHTSA's portal back on October 23, 2026, meaning that said 17-character VINs are also searchable on the automaker's website. All subject vehicles feature the letter K as the first character of the VIN due to South Korean production.
The Venue is the smallest crossover that Hyundai sells in North America, slotting below the Kona. It retails at $20,550 for model year 2026, and prospective customers are presented with a lot of standard kit for this money. The base SE is joined by two additional trim levels, namely the SEL and the SEL with the two-tone roof. All three use a 1.6-liter naturally aspirated I4 with 121 hp on tap.
$22,825 gets you the most affordable Elantra for model year 2026 in the US market, with $25,650 being the entry price of the hybrid. At the very top of the spectrum, the Elantra N currently starts at $35,300 before destination and other taxes. If equipped with the optional wet-clutch DCT, using N Grin Shift mode unlocks a further 10 horsepower for 20 seconds at a time.

This Rustic French Tiny House Is What Makes Tiny Living Wholesome
10 photos
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois
Tiny living is about much more than downsizing, it’s a social movement, a statement, and a lifestyle in its own right, centered around core values such as individual freedom, respect for nature, sustainability, and the return to a simpler life. The tiny house featured in this story was once a simple prototype, but it still embodies the best of tiny living.
No matter how much a tiny house construction business grows over time, its founder will always remember the first tiny home he built and that started it all. Many of the established tiny house companies in various parts of the world started with just a man and his dream, and many people ended up making homes on wheels for other after building one for themselves, simply because they couldn’t find a ready-made house to their liking.
People who built tiny homes can come from very different backgrounds, yet seem to share certain values and passions across cultures and national borders. A deep love for nature and the outdoors, a commitment to sustainability and the wise use of natural resources, a calling for minimalist living, and the desire to help others live their dream as well, are some of the things that these strong, visionary men have in common.
Jean-Maxime is one of them. He is the force behind Tiny and Projet Bois (“Project Wood”), an artisan construction and carpentry workshop in France that was established more than a decade ago, in 2014. Jean-Maxime was passionate about woodwork since the age of 12, but before he turned 30, he took a big decision that changed the trajectory of his life. He felt it was time for a professional reconversion, and he switched gears from environmental engineering to carpentry.
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois Soon after this big step, the young carpenter opened Tiny and Projet Bois in Isere, a beautiful location in the French Alps, and started building custom homes on wheels right away. To this day, his work includes extensive woodwork as well, from staircases to exterior decks and pergolas, and this lifelong passion for wood shows up in the mobile homes he builds as well. Every Tiny &Projet Bois home looks and feels like a wooden paradise where timber comes alive.
Jean-Maxime’s style and capabilities have naturally expanded over time, but he is still very proud of the first house on wheels that he has ever built. This is the prototype, a tiny house that he built almost as an experiment, because he used that project specifically to determine the best materials, to make all the weight assessments and other measurements, and to basically figure things out. This tiny house would become the foundation for all future custom projects.
A tiny house that is born as a prototype has the kind of sentimental value that makes it priceless, even though technically it might be imperfect. What sets this one apart is the rustic gypsy caravan silhouette coupled with a full-wood interior that evokes traditional cabins and farms. It almost feels like a time capsule – a nostalgic home from a bygone era, yet also timeless.
In a time when modern architecture, modern materials, and an industrial approach are taking over, tiny homes like these are a reminder that things can be different and that tiny living is just as much about natural materials and sustainability as it is about affordability and downsizing. There’s a place for container-like tiny homes with steel frames, metal exteriors and chipboard interiors, but there’s also a place for traditional tiny homes on wheels built entirely of wood.
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois The gypsy caravan silhouette gives this prototype tiny house a specific interior look as well, with rounded ceilings and decorative beams. There’s no difference in tone or texture between the wall panels, the ceiling, and the flooring throughout, which gives this home a very unique, cohesive look. The furniture blends in with the walls, and you feel almost enveloped inside a cozy, warm timber cocoon.
One end of the home is dedicated to the lounge area. It has classic windows on two sides – a welcomed break from the oversized picture frames that are almost ubiquitous these days – and mismatched, improvised shelves that add a naïve charm. A large corner sofa takes center stage – it’s welcoming enough for a large group of guests and, most importantly, it can convert into a spacious bed.
The home’s “official” bedroom is the larger loft above the bathroom and kitchen area (there’s also a smaller loft above the lounge, fitted with built-in drawers and only intended for storage). The loft bedroom is big enough to fit a two-person bed, it has windows for cross-ventilation and natural light, and it features a solid cabinet that doubles as a safety wall on the outside.
Access to this loft bedroom is very interesting. It’s not a classic staircase, but not a basic movable ladder either. It looks like a hybrid staircase, but it’s entirely custom-crafted and a bit quirky. The whole structured is built around an actual tree branch extending from the floor to the loft’s edge, and the tiny treads built around it are meant to create a so-called goose-step or duck-step design.
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois The point of this quirky design is to save a great deal of floor space, as the compact treads are places asymmetrically in an alternate order. Indeed, you can tell that this unusual staircase takes up very little space compared to a conventional design, yet it’s still better in terms of safety and comfort than a simple movable ladder. Plus, the rustic charm of that rugged tree branch complements the overall traditional style perfectly.
The kitchen is also a combination of rustic carpentry and modern space efficiency. The cabinetry doesn’t look perfectly aligned, which gives this kitchen the bohemian, a bit chaotic look of many French tiny homes, but it’s meant to offer more storage and greater versatility than its size would suggest. Next to the classic lower cabinets under the countertop, Jean-Maxime added a bespoke cabinet on wheels with multiple drawers and shelves, as well as a modular table.
The modular table serves both as a dining table and a console with built-in storage for the lounge. Classic upper cupboards were ditched in favor of simple open shelves and a tiny rack, which makes room for the classic windows that keep this kitchen bright and airy. Appliances are limited to essentials only: a sink, a stove, and a fridge that is small enough to fit under the countertop, between the cupboards.
This is what minimalism combined with sustainability looks like – real timber comes with the advantage of natural warmth in colder seasons, and modern appliances are integrated into a natural space, instead of taking over. Nothing is perfect, yet there’s more room to breathe. A proper balance between modern glazing and wood paneling keeps this cozy home both luminous and intimate, while timber naturally takes on a decorative role in addition to pure functionality.

Segway Drops "Road-Legal" Xyber Air Class 3 E-Bike – Costs a Third Less Than Its Powerful Cousin
21 photos
Photo: Segway Inc.
At the 2025 CES, Segway unveiled the Xyber, an e-bike that is able to reach a peak of 43 mph, can handle two battery packs with a wild 112-mile range, but also a price tag of $3,000. Well, Segway has chosen to drop a new Xyber version, one that’s lighter, more legal, and less expensive.
It’s called the Xyber Air, and while it shares the moto-like spirit of the Xyber, it is a completely different two-wheeler. The Air, as its name would imply, is designed to be a stripped-down version of the Xyber, and this means a striking and unmistakable Segway design, countless safety and personalization features, and ample power to stay within legal road limits.
To give it this unmistakable Segway look, components like the fender, saddle, and even the frame have seen the touch of Segway designers and continues the motorcycle-like look of the class.
Photo: Segway Inc. At its core, the Air is powered by a 750 W (1,600 W peak) motor that grants us access to a top speed of as much as 28 mph (45 kph), marking it as a Class 3 e-bike. That motor can also produce a whopping 80 Nm (59 lb-ft) of torque, plenty to tackle hills in our towns and reach 20 mph from a standstill in just 6 seconds.
Compared to the more powerful Xyber, the Air hits this speed in over twice the time; the classic version does this in 2.7 seconds. A cadence and gyroscopic sensor manage power flow.
This motor is strapped to the rear wheel of the Air and drawing power from a battery mounted into the upper section of the bike. Overall, 717 Wh of juice is available to us here, granting us access to as much as 58 miles (93 km). Not bad, if you ask me. Once drained, the Air can take up to 6.5 hours before you’re back on the road.
In some of the images in the gallery, we can see the lower section of the bike is occupied by what can be mistaken as a battery but it's a hardshell, in-frame storage bag. Keep that in mind.
Photo: Segway Inc. One difference that I can see is that the Air can’t handle a second battery like the standard Xyber, at least, not loaded directly onto the frame, but you can always grab another pack and have it ready to go to double your ride time.
More on the performance side of the story, I need to point out that the Air is sporting a pair of hydraulic brakes with two pistons per 180 mm disc, but it’s what’s on the electronic side of things that matter most.
According to Segway’s website, the Air, just like the classic Xyber, is equipped with Hill Start and Descent control, but it’s the Traction Control System that matters most, which continuously monitors wheel slip and in case of loss of traction, motor input is regulated in order to stabilize it once again.
In the comfort department, allow me to point out that the Air is rocking features like a suspension fork at the front, reducing bumps and vibrations with 80 mm of travel, the ultra-fat tires for more added comfort and grip with the road. Under the right pressure, fat tires are also suitable for terrains like snow and sand. An IPX7 rating ensure that you don’t have any issues with water and snow.
Photo: Segway Inc. But, we’re still not done here. The Air includes an auto unlocking feature, GPS that works with Apple Find My, and a Lost Mode, that allows you to cut function in case someone does manage to steal it. A motion sensor and alarm are in place too, so if you’re nearby, you can hear it.
The rest of the Air includes that ample and signature lighting that Segway is using across a wide range of their products, making it easier to see and be seen at night, and a display that links to your phone and even lets you answer calls without having to dig into your pocket to do so.
The latter also allows us to keep tabs on ride times, battery charge, speed, and other diagnostics that you need to be aware of. Brightness is automatically adjusted depending on the ambient lighting and you can even sync with health and fitness apps. What more do you want?
Photo: Segway Inc. All that makes up for an e-bike that weighs as much as 86 lbs (39 kg) and has a peak load of 330 lbs (150 kg), while being able to support riders as tall as 6 ft. Just keep in mind that scrambler-style bikes such as these come with a bit of a drawback for taller riders: limited distance between the saddle and bottom bracket; a full and proper extension of the leg isn't so possible.
Currently, there are four reviews for the Xyber Air , and it carries a full five out of five stars, but it’s only been around for a few days now. In time, we should be able to gauge market happiness better. The standard Xyber, after over a year of use, is showcasing a 3.9 star out of five rating.
With EICMA around the corner here and autoevolution attending the show, be sure that we’ll be stopping by the Segway stand to see what this crew has in store for the upcoming year; you can bet an Air will be there.

Segway Drops a Fresh E-Scooter for the New Rider – Costs $550 and Aimed at Urban Landscapes
14 photos
Photo: Segway Inc.
Hate on them all you want, e-scooters are here to stay, and teams like Segway are still cranking out what they feel is the perfect option for leaving your car at home. One such option is this brand’s latest E3 Go, an urban-ready, last-mile solution that could be the answer to saving some gas.
If you head over to Segway’s website, the E3 Go is currently selling for as little $550 (€500), marking it as one of the more affordable options from this brand. Time to find out what this one has in store and if it’s for you.
As a Segway mobility product , a particular design language is in place, along with the colors chosen for systems and components on the E3. The fork covers are a clear Segway trait, along with red wiring and integrated headlight. That red circle around the hub bolt is also a signature trait of this brand’s e-scooters.
Photo: Segway Inc. According to details posted on Segway’s website, the E3 is sporting a 400 W motor with a peak of up to 800 W, granting us access to a top speed of up to 20 mph (32 kph). It’s not the fastest on the market, and the reason being is that Segway positions this one as an entry-level option aimed at the new rider.
While we don’t have a specific number on torque, it is capable of handling up to 18% inclines, plenty to tackle just about every slope in your town. Sure, there are some limits, but most cities are on the menu. Rear-wheel drive is used here too, and it’s a bit trickier to handle off-road.
Since cities are rarely perfect, Segway has also chosen to add some vibration-reducing properties to the E3, part of which is the dual-arm, coil suspension at the front with 40 mm of travel. Couple that with tubeless pneumatic tires, and we have two sources of softness.
Keep in mind that this setup is not one that’s designed to handle off-road use, so be sure to stick to tarmac with this option.
Photo: Segway Inc. Off-road riding, if you do choose to entertain, is going to drain the battery much faster, which isn’t the largest around, so you’ll need to actually keep tabs on how far you decide to ride.
Segway’s website mentions that just 276 Wh of juice is in the battery that’s integrated into the deck. This is only good enough for a peak of 25 miles (40 km) in Eco mode, and if you do decide to fly around at a full 20 mph, only 11 miles (18 km) is to be expected. It is a true last-mile solution indeed.
Charging this small battery takes surprisingly long, with a manufacturer-reported downtime of 5.5 hours. While that is quite a while for a battery this small, it still ensures that you can recharge while you’re at work.
A couple of systems that are in place on the E3 are very similar to what we find on other Segway products, including traction control that feels traction loss and adjusts power, to regain it. and a better wheel trail to keep the scooter stable at higher speeds.
Photo: Segway Inc. Two sources of braking also help keep things in control while riding around, including a drum brake at the front, and at the rear, the motor-resistance is the second.
More in the safety department, we can look to the BMS that Segway adds to the with eight different layers of protection in order to ensure that you don’t worry about your house catching on fire while you’re charging and ensure a longer battery life.
Furthermore, lighting at the front and rear ensures that you’re easily seen, even at night, but there are also turn signals in place here, letting other riders and vehicle owners know your intentions out there.
As an e-scooter that’s aimed at the urban landscape, Segway did integrate a folding frame into the works, allowing us to easily store the E3 in the corner of a room but also make it easier to take up a flight of stairs too. This mechanism can be activated with a single hand.
Photo: Segway Inc. Weight sits at a bit above 46 lbs (21 kg), so you can skip the gym for this one. Max payload sits at 220 lbs (100 kg), so for larger riders, this one is off the menu. Toss in an app, Find My compatibility, and an LED display, and we have ourselves an E3.
All you need now is $550 in your pocket, a test ride, and before long, you have a decision to make. Clearly, it’s not for everyone, but for the new rider, the E3 Go does appear to be rather promising.
Lat but not least, we’ll be attending EICMA for 2026, and Segway is sure to be there, so stick around for more news from this brand and what’s in store for the new year. The Powersports lineup has something special in place.

Triple-Black 1971 Plymouth Cuda Sells for $385K, Sets Record for V-Code Hardtops
18 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Mecum's Dallas/Fort Worth 2026 auction just ended on October 24, with hundreds of modern and classic vehicles changing hands over the course of four days. The event saw several high-profile muscle cars going under the hammer, with a 1971 Plymouth Cuda netting well over $300,000.
Specifically, the all-black Cuda you see here crossed the block for $385,000, a figure that also includes the buyer's premium. The selling price makes it the seventh most expensive vehicle auctioned off at the event. It's also the most expensive classic that's still factory stock (a 1969 Road Runner restomod fetched $407,000).
Despite the high sticker, this Cuda doesn't have a 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi. However, it does have the next best thing under the hood. I'm talking about the 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) Six-Barrel V8, which, much like the Hemi, was discontinued after the 1971 model year. And Plymouth didn't sell many cars equipped with this engine either.
Barracuda deliveries dropped to only 16,492 units in 1971. Only a quarter of these cars were high-performance Cuda models, and most of them rolled off the assembly line with the standard 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) big-block or the 340-cubic-inch (5.6-liter) small-block.
The Hemi, which made the Cuda very expensive to insure, found its way into only 114 cars. The 440 Six-Barrel wasn't notably more popular either; only 254 customers opted for this powerplant. This Cuda is one of those cars, sporting the correct V code in the VIN sequence. But the production number is actually much lower.
It's all due to the four-speed manual gearbox, which was paired with only 113 Six-Barrel engines. Five of these cars were convertibles, so we're looking at one of only 108 hardtops fitted with this drivetrain combo.
I could also factor in the triple-black color combo , but I don't have specific production figures to run by. But I do know that black wasn't a popular choice at the time, and I'm willing to bet that fewer than 10 cars were ordered with this exact color/drivetrain setup. Oh, did I also mention that it's a Super Track Pak car?
This means that the 390-horsepower V8 mates with a Dana 60 rear axle with 4.10 gears. In short, this Mopar will be at home on the drag strip if you're into quarter-mile runs.
As expected from a classic that sold for over $300,000, this Cuda has a numbers-matching drivetrain. It also shows only 34,349 miles (55,279 km) on the odometer and comes with the original broadcast sheet.
The selling price sets a new benchmark for V-code hardtops. At $385,000, this Cuda outsold a different four-speed Six-Barrel example that went under the hammer for $363,000 earlier in 2026. However, it's not the most expensive 1971 V-code Cuda, as a convertible changed hands for $1.15 million, while a second one traded for $962,500.
Speaking of million-dollar cars, Dallas/Fort Worth 2026 saw a 2006 Ford GT Heritage Edition top the sales chart with a $1.67 million sticker. The top three was completed by a 2026 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X Stars & Steel Edition ($550,000) and a 2027 Corvette ZR1X 3LZ Convertible ($495,000).

This Is the Plymouth Barracuda That Chrysler Never Built but Wished It Did
25 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
The Chrysler Corporation has never built a four-door Plymouth Barracuda, even though it flirted with the idea for years. But a renowned Mopar restoration expert did. He spent roughly four years and an estimated 10,000 man-hours, engineering and hand-fabricating this showstopper.
All Plymouth Barracudas produced by the Chrysler Corporation from 1964 to 1973 were either two-door coupes or convertibles. However, Chrysler designers did seriously consider rolling out one and even came up with a four-door E-body mockup clay model in the late 1960s.
The auto giant's executives wanted to anticipate the future, trying to figure out if a potential four-door could compete with the high-end European sports sedans of the era. The full-scale prototype that was presented to them behind closed doors featured shorter front doors, functional rear doors, and a slightly altered roofline to allow for rear-seat headroom, much like the four-door custom build that is now being auctioned off through Bring a Trailer.
Back in the 1960s, executives eventually determined that the costs to manufacture unique rear doors, glass, and quarter panels would not be profitable for a low-volume sedan. The four-door never got the green light, and they had to permanently scrap the project.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Fast forward to 2016, and a four-door Plymouth Barracuda was exhibited at the 2016 SEMA Show, where it was also entered into the event’s prestigious Battle of the Builders competition. Because it was meticulously protected and treated like a flawless museum-quality build, its tires never actually touched the road pavement from its initial SEMA debut until 2022.
Finally out of storage six years after SEMA That was when the four-door Plymouth Barracuda made headlines, finally coming out of its long-term storage. In October 2022, it was finally rolled out just to be photographed , filmed, and officially presented to the public as a functional, running vehicle. However, now, it has only one mile on the clock, which proves it has been a garage queen all its life, stored away from the eyes of the curious.
This car is the creation of Dave Walden, a renowned custom car builder, Mopar restorer, and the founder of ECS Automotive Concepts. He and his team spent four years and an estimated 10,000 man-hours to build the four-door Barracuda.
Because the Chrysler Corporation never made a four-door E-body , the team couldn't simply go out and buy off-the-shelf parts, so they had to come up with a manufacturing process that mirrored the 1970s factory products.
Photo: Bring a Trailer The most challenging part of the build was adding two doors without ruining the iconic, low-slung silhouette of the Barracuda. They began with a standard 1970 Plymouth donor car, cut the chassis, and precisely lengthened the body by 10 inches to make room for an extra pair of doors and a functional rear seating area.
To prevent the car from looking like an odd stretched limousine, the team hand-fabricated entirely custom steel rear doors and inner door jambs, while using the structural B-pillars from a Dodge Coronet sedan. A standard Barracuda roof tapers aggressively toward the decklid.
To ensure the rear passengers actually had enough headroom and did not have to sit contorted in bizarre positions, Dave Walden's team entirely reconstructed the roofline, altering the pitch of the C-pillars and blending them into the stock quarter panels.
Instead of using modern glass, Dave Walden and his team sourced custom, date-coded windows specifically cut to match the newly fabricated four-door dimensions, complete with authentic factory safety stamps.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Walden was famous for his obsessive attention to historical accuracy. The mechanical assembly of the car was handled with a strict restoration-first mindset and did not allow a single deviation unless it was critically necessary.
Red paint and a black vinyl top over a black vinyl interior The car was finished in a flawless Rallye Red, paint code FE5, and equipped with a custom black vinyl roof, stretched and fitted over the elongated body, hiding the seamless weld points where the body had been stretched. The Barracuda sits on 14-inch wheels, wrapped in F70-14 Goodyear red-line tires.
The Barracuda's cabin hosts period-correct bench seats upholstered in black vinyl. The woodgrain-rimmed steering wheel sits on a unique tilting and telescoping steering column, framing an instrument cluster that integrates a speedometer scaled up to 120 mph, a clock, and gauges that indicate fuel level, coolant temperature, and alternator status.
Under the hood of the Barracuda, he slid a period-correct, high-performance 340-cubic-inch (5.6-liter) E55 LA V8 engine , with a Carter four-barrel carburetor set up atop a factory-spec intake manifold. The V8 was factory-rated at 275 horsepower (279 metric horsepower) and 340 pound-feet (461 Newton meters) of torque.
Photo: Bring a Trailer A fully rebuilt 727 TorqueFlite three-speed automatic transmission put the power down through the rear wheels. The car features power steering, while power front disc brakes and rear drums provide the stopping power. Though, given its mileage, it has hardly had the chance to use them.
Every single bolt, clamp, and bracket utilized original assembly markings. The underside of the chassis, engine bay, and suspension components were intentionally hit with the exact paint dabs, chalk marks, and inspection stamps that a factory Barracuda would have received on the assembly line in 1970.
To complete the illusion of a real four-door Plymouth Barracuda , Dave Walden created a fully customized, historically accurate window sticker and assembly broadcast sheet, detailing the pricing and options for the phantom build.
Following the passing of its creator, Dave Walden, in 2019, the sedan has been carefully preserved and was only taken out in October 2022 before a public sale. It crossed the auction block at the Mecum Kissimmee event in January 2023, when someone paid $121,000 to take it home.
Photo: Bring a Trailer That owner sold it again at the Kruse Auctions Auburn Fall Event for less than half that sum: $54,880. Now, it is going under the hammer once again on Bring a Trailer, with the odometer still indicating just one mile and a Pennsylvania title that classifies it as a 1970 Plymouth Barracuda four-door. With six days to go, the highest bid reached $40,000.

18 photos
Photo: IIHS on YouTube
As you're well aware, the A7-generation Jetta is getting on a bit. Introduced for the 2019 model year in the US market, Volkswagen's compact sedan has racked up two "good" ratings from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety for its performance in the small and moderate overlap crash tests.
The updated moderate overlap test recreates a frontal collision in which part of the Jetta's front end strikes a barrier. Both the structure and safety cell earn "good" marks, and so do the driver's chest, head and neck, thigh, and hip protection, along with the driver's restraint performance. Only the leg and foot protection slips to "acceptable," which isn't bad at all for a design this old.
Per the nonprofit organization's report, 2.4 inches of intrusion were recorded in the left side of the footwell, along with 1.6 in the center and 0.8 on the right. The A-pillar held its position as intended, and the instrument panel did not move rearward. At the rear, the occupant behind the driver approaches the front seatback during the impact. While this increases the potential for a head injury, the moderate test recorded no head contact with the front seatback.
The 2027 model year Jetta further earns "good" ratings in both the driver- and passenger-side small overlap evaluations. According to the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety , the Jetta isn't worthy of anything higher than "acceptable" in the side impact test. The structure and safety cell both scored "good," yet driver and rear passenger pelvis protection were deemed "marginal."
Driver pelvis protection and rear occupant torso protection fell to "marginal," preventing the side test from living up to the expectations set by the frontal evaluations. The bad news continues with headlight performance, which earned the "marginal" rating across every single trim available for 2027.
Photo: IIHS on YouTube Equipped with LED reflectors that also feature high-beam assistance, the Jetta offers inadequate low-beam visibility on both left curves and inadequate high-beam visibility in multiple scenarios. Thankfully, the low beams never exceeded the nonprofit organization's glare limits. On the AEB front, automatic braking has a particular blind spot.
The Jetta avoids a collision with a crossing child at 12 miles per hour. Step up to 25, and it reduces impact speed by 12 miles per hour. In nighttime automatic braking tests involving a crossing adult, it avoids a collision at 12 and cuts impact speed by up to 18 miles per hour in the 25-mph test.
Its weak point becomes clear when an adult walks parallel to the road. In this scenario, the Jetta fails to slow in the 25-mph, regardless of whether it uses the high or low beams. At 37 miles per hour, which is nearly 60 clicks in European speak, it fails to slow yet again. The system, however, issues a warning at the moment of impact rather than giving the driver some time to react.
Even the child seat hardware couldn't do better than "acceptable" by IIHS standards. The safety boffins claim that it's difficult to maneuver around the lower anchors of both outboard rear seats. Even though it does show its age from the standpoint of safety, the Jetta remains a nicely equipped compact with an enticing MSRP. The 158-hp sedan presently starts at $23,995 sans destination.
Just like the 1.5-liter turbo grades, the GLI also comes with two pedals. The manual was dropped for model year 2027, marking the end of an era for the Volkswagen brand in the US market. Positioned below the Golf GTI, the Jetta GLI will set you back $33,795 from the outset. Instead of an eight-speed auto, a dual-clutch box with seven forward ratios is featured.

He Bought a Nissan GT-R NISMO and Parked It. Two Years Later, He Is Selling It With Just 500 Miles
11 photos
Photo: George J Saliba | YouTube
The owner of this 2023 Nissan GT-R NISMO bought the car at an auction back in 2024 with 96 miles and is selling it after a couple of drives with roughly 500 miles on the clock. This year, he paid $3,000 for the insurance and hasn’t driven it once. So for him, the rare Nissan is basically a money pit. However, he took it to a dealership and hopes to cash in.
Just 547 miles or 880 kilometers. This is how far this 2023 Nissan GT-R NISMO has traveled since it rolled off the production line of the Tochigi Plant in Kaminokawa, Tochigi, Japan, three years ago. For the rest of the time, it was locked in a garage, while its chances of hitting the road are becoming ever slimmer.
Painted Jet Black Pearl paint code: GAG over a NISMO Black and Red interior in leather, which wraps the Recaro seats and door panels, the GT-R rides on 20-inch Rays wheels finished in metallic black with a red accent stripe along the outer lip, shod with Dunlop high-performance summer tires.
The owner of this 2023 Nissan GT-R NISMO took his car to a dealership in Ewing, New Jersey, along with the auction poster. Yes, he bought it at auction two years ago. He wears a T-shirt that shows his love for the R34. He had one, modified it, and eventually sold it.
Photo: George J Saliba | YouTube He has been nostalgic about it since. He had been flirting with the idea of buying one again, and he found it at a Barrett-Jackson auction in 2024, when he celebrated his father’s 70th birthday at the event. When the GT-R was auctioned, he got up on stage, placed the winning bid, and took it home.
He tinted the side windows and windshield “probably three times” and PPF-ed the front bumper. It sounds like he was planning to drive it. But things did not really go according to plan. He took his wife to the beach and went to a wedding in it, soon after he purchased it. Then he parked it and never touched it again.
He is only the second owner of the car. The GT-R had 96 miles (155 kilometers) on the clock when he bought it and is selling it with 547 miles. With that sort of ultra-low mileage, “I feel bad driving it,” he explains. He believes the time has come for it to go to someone else who will actually drive it.
How generous of him, isn't it? However, when the owner of the dealership asks him if he would be selling it for $250,000, he says he wants an extra $100,000. So the car won't be going anywhere for anything under $350,000.
Photo: George J Saliba | YouTube The 2023 Nissan GT-R NISMO hit the U.S. market with a starting price of $210,740, plus a $1,895 destination and handling charge. Nowadays, the model breaks the rules of vehicle depreciation. On the used car market, it commands a significant premium over the MSRP, selling for anything between $286,000 and $312,000.
Very low-mileage, all-original cars can go well beyond the $400,000 mark, and it makes complete sense nowadays. Across the world, total GT-R production run for the 2023 model year was capped at roughly 1,500 units.
Out of those 1,500 cars sold worldwide, only about 300 were built as the range-topping NISMO variant . A significant portion of production stayed in Japan. It is estimated that fewer than 100 units of the 2023 GT-R NISMO made it to the United States.
The Japan-made model is powered by the 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged V6, code-named VR38DETT, and fitted with GT3 racecar-derived turbochargers. Every single V6 in every single GT-R is completely hand-assembled from scratch by a select group of just nine master craftsmen, known as Takumi, at Nissan's Yokohama plant. Each engine takes roughly six hours to build.
Photo: George J Saliba | YouTube When it is completed, it pushes out 600 horsepower (608 metric horsepower) and 481 pound-feet (652 Newton meters) of torque. Those are enough to make the car rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in just 2.9 seconds, run the quarter mile in 10.8 seconds, with a trap speed of 128 mph (206 kph) and max out at 205 mph (330 kph). Those were numbers that helped it battle neck to neck with Ferraris and Lamborghinis at the track.
Nissan phased out the R35 GT-R that built a huge car cult around it, and that has been affectionately called Godzilla during its historic 18-year run. The automaker stopped taking orders for the model in Japan in March 2025. The final R35 GT-R, a Premium spec finished in Midnight Purple, rolled off the production line of the Tochigi plant on August 26, 2025, officially ending the production of the legendary model.
So, the only way for enthusiasts to get their hands on a Nissan GT-R NISMO, or any GT-R for that matter, is the used car market, where these cars come with prices that often go much above the sticker.
If the dealership pays $350,000 for the car, it will most likely add a solid premium when listing it for sale. The future owner has two scenarios: lock it inside the garage like owner number 1 and owner number 2 did or drive it until its wheels fall off. What would you do?

Audi Will Build SUVs in America in a $4 Billion Plant
7 photos
Photo: Audi
Audi officially announced a $4 billion investment to build its first-ever assembly plant in the United States. The German automaker chose the Middle Georgia Megasite in Peach County, Georgia, for the future facility, which is expected to build roughly 200,000 SUVs per year.
Audi currently has no manufacturing or assembly plant in the United States. Up until this point, it is the only major German luxury automaker without a U.S. factory, unlike its main competitors. BMW builds X-branded SUVs in South Carolina, while Mercedes-Benz rolls out the GLE and GLE Coupe, the GLS, the Maybach GLS, the EQS, and EQS SUVs in Alabama.
The move, announced by U.S. President Donald Trump himself at a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia, represents a major strategic shift for Audi, which has been hit hard by import tariffs since it previously shipped all its vehicles sold in the American market from Europe and Mexico.
"We are planning to bring our biggest and most premium SUVs and produce them here in Macon, Georgia,” said Audi CEO Gernot Dollner, standing on the stage next to President Trump, who pledged to force automakers to relocate their production for the American market to the U.S.
Photo: Audi The announcement comes just nine days before the November 3 midterm elections. Referred to as a $4.2 billion investment by President Trump, the upcoming Audi plant is expected to generate roughly 4,500 jobs for the Middle Georgia region, with thousands more expected via suppliers and logistics partners.
The plant should have an annual output of up to 200,000 vehicles. First and foremost, the facility will specialize in building Audi’s largest premium flagship SUVs, such as the Q7, Q8, and the recently unveiled Q9 , tailored specifically for North American consumers.
Right now, Audi is building its high-riding models in Bratislava, Slovakia, where the Q7 and the Q8 see the light of day, the Q5 in San Jose Chiapa, Mexico, the electric Q4 and Q6 e-tron in Ingolstadt, Zwickau, and Brussels, while the Q3 comes to life in Gyor, Hungary.
Construction is scheduled to begin sometime in 2027, with vehicle production officially kicking off in the early 2030s, Automotive News reports . With this move, Audi is trying to offset the effects of the tariffs imposed by the Trump administration.
Photo: Audi According to Reuters, in 2025 alone, U.S. import tariffs cost Audi an estimated $1.4 billion. Establishing local manufacturing will shield Audi from trade volatility and will help its parent company, Volkswagen Group, extend its footprint in North America. The auto giant already has a plant in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and is building the Scout Motors site in South Carolina.
In the meantime, Audi is in full swing to restructure its production in Europe and is struggling with sales figures in free fall in the United States. Audi sold 107,667 cars in the U.S. from January to September 2026, which is down 16% compared to the same period of 2025.
